translation: Pallavi (Chorus): O girl... you girl walking away in a red saree, who are you, dear, who are you? From which village, girl, have you come to our village, and why, dear — won't you tell me a little? (You girl walking away in a red saree, who are you, dear, who are you?) (From which village, girl, have you come to our village, and why, dear — won't you tell me a little?)

Verse 1: What is your village called, what is your name, dear, O lady, my Satyabhama? Swear on your pearl necklace and tell me, my darling, my rubber doll. (What is your village called, what is your name, dear, O lady, my Satyabhama?) (Swear on your pearl necklace and tell me, my darling, my rubber doll.) (You girl walking away in a red saree...)

Verse 2: Glancing my way and swaying your waist, O girl, my rasgulla, you've hollowed out my heart and now you're walking away — where to, dear, my rose branch? (Glancing my way and swaying your waist, O girl, my rasgulla) (You've hollowed out my heart and now you're walking away — where to, dear, my rose branch?) (You girl walking away in a red saree...)

Verse 3: All your curves and graces, all your tender young charms, O darling, my clever beauty — they are jaaji jasmines, dear, creeper jasmines, my moon, my doll of youth. (All your curves and graces, all your tender young charms, O darling, my clever beauty) (They are jaaji jasmines, dear, creeper jasmines, my moon, my doll of youth) (You girl walking away in a red saree...)

Verse 4: Seeing you, my heart refuses to stay still, girl, O Rekha, my Sasirekha. Seeing the golden treasures behind your colourful blouse — such coyness, O Madhubala! (Seeing you, my heart refuses to stay still, girl, O Rekha, my Sasirekha) (Seeing the golden treasures behind your colourful blouse — such coyness, O Madhubala!) (You girl walking away in a red saree...)

Verse 5: Seeing the colour of your lips, like the flame-of-the-forest flower, O parrot, my parakeet — why don't you answer, girl, no matter how much I call, O my little pulley-wheel, my sprout of love? (Seeing the colour of your lips, like the flame-of-the-forest flower, O parrot, my parakeet) (Why don't you answer, girl, no matter how much I call, O my little pulley-wheel, my sprout of love?) (You girl walking away in a red saree...)
summaryEn:
A young man's flirtatious song to a stranger: a girl in a red saree who walks through his village and away again. He fires questions at her — which village she is from, what her name is, why she has come — and begs her to swear on her pearl necklace and answer. As she ignores him, his praise grows more and more extravagant. He compares her to Satyabhama, the proud queen of Krishna in the epics, and to Sasirekha, and he calls her Madhubala and Rekha. He also likens her to sweets (rasgulla), flowers (a rose branch, jaaji and creeper jasmines, the red modugu or flame-of-the-forest blossom) and a chattering parakeet.

The song is built on rhyming endearments at the end of each half-line — bhama and Satyabhama, pilla and rasagulla, jaana and nerajaana, chilaka, gilaka and molaka — which give it a bouncy, teasing rhythm. Every verse is sung twice and then leads back into the red-saree refrain. Everyday Telangana speech mixes with borrowed words like 'rabbari' (rubber) and 'jawani' (youth), which gives the song a playful, modern-village feel.

తన ఊరి మీదుగా ఎర్ర చీర కట్టుకుని వెళ్లిపోతున్న తెలియని పిల్లను చూసి ఒక యువకుడు పాడే సరదా పాట ఇది. ఏ ఊరు, నీ పేరేంటి, మా ఊరికి ఎందుకొచ్చావు అని ప్రశ్నలు గుప్పిస్తూ, ముత్యాల దండ మీద ఒట్టేసి చెప్పమని బతిమాలుతాడు. ఆమె పలకకపోవడంతో అతని పొగడ్తలు మరింత పెరుగుతాయి. ఆమెను కృష్ణుడి భార్య సత్యభామతో, శశిరేఖతో పోల్చుతాడు, మధుబాల, రేఖ అని పిలుస్తాడు; రసగుల్లా, గులాబీ కొమ్మ, జాజి మల్లెలు, తీగ మల్లెలు, మోదుగు పువ్వు, రామచిలుక వంటి పోలికలతో ఆమె అందాన్ని వర్ణిస్తాడు.

ప్రతి పాదం చివర భామ–సత్యభామ, పిల్లా–రసగుల్లా, జానా–నెరజాణ, చిలకా–గిలకా–మొలకా వంటి ప్రాస పదాలు రావడం వల్ల పాటకు చిలిపి, ఊపున్న లయ వస్తుంది. ప్రతి చరణం రెండుసార్లు పాడి మళ్లీ ‘ఎర్ర చీర కట్టుకోని’ పల్లవికి తిరిగి వస్తారు. తెలంగాణ వాడుక భాషలో ‘రబ్బారి బొమ్మ’, ‘జవానీ బొమ్మ’ వంటి అన్యభాషా పదాలు కలవడం పాటకు ఆధునిక పల్లె సరదా రంగును ఇస్తుంది.
